task: Finalize these loan-handling procedures for Bellweather Archive's receiving and dispatch teams.
source_facts: Bellweather Archive, its register, and all handling rules are synthetic and authoritative. A loaned object arrives in a reusable crate with an external shock indicator. Receiving and return preparation are separate procedures, usually performed weeks apart by different teams. A shift lead prints only the relevant procedure as a work card; neither team can assume the other card is attached. For each procedure, place the printed loan record beside the crate before handling it, assign two staff members to handle the object, and prepare a clean padded table before moving the object. These prerequisites are required locally on each work card. For receipt, photograph the unopened crate before opening it. A red incoming shock indicator requires the receiving team to stop before opening the crate. After the crate passes that check and is opened, take an arrival-condition photograph of the object. Record the object's arrival condition in the loan register, using the identifier on the printed loan record. A condition discrepancy requires lender approval before shelving. The assigned storage shelf is C-4 and must be entered in the register. For return preparation, compare the object with its arrival-condition photograph before packing. Lender approval is required before sealing the return crate. Place a signed condition sheet in the return packet, fit a new shock indicator to the crate, and obtain the carrier's signature in the pickup log at handover. The object's arrival photograph and condition entry create the reference used for the later comparison. The record beside the crate identifies the loan and prevents reliance on memory when more than one crate is present. The padded table is the object's staging surface, not a replacement for two-person handling. The return packet travels with the crate; the pickup log remains with the archive. In the draft, the two adjacent instructions to enter C-4 into the same register field describe one action and contain a removable restatement.
draft:
# Bellweather Archive loan work cards

Use the work card for the activity assigned to the current shift. Receiving establishes an arrival record; return preparation uses that record to compare the object before it leaves the archive. The two activities can occur weeks apart and involve different staff.

## Receive a loan

### Set up the receiving station

Place the printed loan record beside the crate before handling it. This gives the receiving team a visible loan identity when several crates are nearby. Assign two staff members to handle the object. Prepare a clean padded table before moving the object; the staging surface does not replace the second handler.

Use the identifier on the printed loan record for the register entry, rather than a name or destination remembered from an earlier conversation.

### Inspect and record

Photograph the unopened crate before opening it. Check the external shock indicator. If the indicator is red, stop before opening the crate. This check happens while the crate is still in its arrival state, so the initial photograph and indicator observation refer to the same stage of handling.

After the crate passes that check and is opened, take an arrival-condition photograph of the object. Record the object's arrival condition in the loan register. The arrival record will be used during return preparation, so it should describe the condition at receipt rather than an expected condition copied from memory. If there is a condition discrepancy, obtain lender approval before shelving the object.

Record the assigned shelf as C-4 in the register. The register's shelf field should therefore contain C-4. The shelf entry associates the recorded object with its storage location after receipt.

## Prepare a return

### Set up the return station

Place the printed loan record beside the crate before handling it. Use that visible record to identify the loan being returned. Assign two staff members to handle the object. Prepare a clean padded table before moving the object, even if the incoming team previously used a padded surface at receipt. This is a new handling session with its own setup.

### Compare and pack

Compare the object with its arrival-condition photograph before packing. The photograph is the reference created during receipt, rather than an illustration of how the object is supposed to look. Use the comparison to establish the condition being presented for return.

Obtain lender approval before sealing the return crate. Place a signed condition sheet in the return packet so the condition documentation travels with the crate.

Fit a new shock indicator to the crate. At handover, obtain the carrier's signature in the pickup log. Keep that log with the archive as its handover record.
